module_name: Ancient India: Early Humans and the Indus Valley Civilisation

extracted_notes.text: Based on coalescence of Mitochondrial DNA and Y Chromosome data, it is thought that the earliest extant lineages of anatomically modern humans or Homo sapiens on the Indian subcontinent had reached there from Africa between 80,000 and 50,000 years ago, and with high likelihood by 55,000 years ago.
Their long occupation, initially in varying forms of isolation as hunter-gatherers, has made the region highly diverse, second only to Africa in human genetic diversity.
Evidence for the neolithic period in the western margins of the Indus river basin, at Mehrgarh in Balochistan, Pakistan, dates to after 7000 BCE.
Domestication of grain-producing plants (including barley) and animals (including humped zebu cattle) occurred here.
These cultures gradually evolved into the Indus Valley Civilisation, which flourished during 2500-1900 BCE in Pakistan and western India.

Centred around cities such as Mohenjo-daro, Harappa, Dholavira, Ganweriwala, and Rakhigarhi, its characteristic features included standardised weights, steatite seals, a written script, urban planning, public works, and arts and crafts including pottery styles, terracotta human figures and animal statuettes.

phase_1_deduplicator_report.editorial_rationale: I have pruned the proposed widgets to eliminate redundancy while maintaining a comprehensive visual experience. First, I addressed the conflict over the timeline of early humans and the IVC (n1, n3, n5). raw_w0 (fact_grid) was kept as it synthesizes multiple dates into a single structural view, while raw_w7, raw_w9, and raw_w10 (insight_badges) were removed as they are simple repetitions of the same data points. Second, for the cities of the IVC (n6), raw_w1 (entity_profiles) was chosen over raw_w5 (itemized_breakdown) because entity profiles provide a more complex and visually engaging way to represent key hubs. Third, for the features of the IVC (n6), raw_w4 (itemized_breakdown) was kept over raw_w11 (fact_grid) because a bulleted list is a more natural way to present a diverse set of characteristic features than a qualitative grid. raw_w6 was removed as it failed its own internal requirement for a minimum of 3 items. raw_w2 (before_and_after) was kept because it provides a unique comparative angle on the evolution from Neolithic to Urban, which is distinct from the simple listing of dates. raw_w3 (jargon_buster) and raw_w8 (insight_badge) were kept as they provide unique information (definition of Homo sapiens and genetic diversity) that does not conflict with any other widget.
